clips.text: One man. Long coat, in this heat. He pointed something at the roses, there was a flash, and when I could see again, there was that.
clips.script: [crisp, disapproving] One man. [dry] Long coat, in this heat. [measured, reporting] He pointed something at the roses, there was a flash, [flat, gesturing] and when I could see again, there was THAT.

clips.text: I held it up to the lamp. There's a piano on it.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, conspiratorial] I held it up to the lamp. [warm Long Island accent, intrigued] There's a PIANO on it.

clips.text: Why didn't he jump?
clips.script: [puzzled, disappointed] Why didn't he JUMP?

clips.text: And the red's gone out of everything around it. The roses, the lawn, my good hose. All grey.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, bitter, aggrieved] And the red's gone out of everything around it. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, pained, listing] The roses, the lawn, my good HOSE. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, flat, hurt] All grey.

clips.text: ...and I only caught him because the hat kept getting taller. Where'd the muffins go?
clips.script: [thick New York accent, finishing his story, pleased, has noticed nothing] ...and I only caught him because the hat kept getting TALLER. [thick New York accent, mild, puzzled] Where'd the muffins go?

clips.text: ...wait. You're very tall. Are you a squirrel?
clips.script: [puzzled, tiny] ...wait. You're very TALL. [suspicious, squeaky] Are you a squirrel?

clips.text: You're following them with a salad spinner.
clips.script: [flat, incredulous] You're following them with a SALAD SPINNER.

clips.text: She can get in line. She owes me a couch.
clips.script: [dry, quick] She can get in line. [wry, deadpan] She owes me a COUCH.

clips.text: And this one is drinking purple soda before noon.
clips.script: [dry, sidelong] And THIS one is drinking purple soda before noon.

clips.text: First it's one little flame. Then it's music. Then people have friends over. I've seen where it goes.
clips.script: [ominous, soggy] First it's one little flame. [darker, building] Then it's music. [grim] Then people have friends over. [flat, haunted] I've seen where it goes.

clips.text: That makes it worse. Do you have it in white? With the crusts cut off?
clips.script: [prissy, appalled] That makes it WORSE. [hopeful, demanding] Do you have it in white? [petulant] With the crusts cut off?

clips.text: I couldn't pull the one at the pond out either. ...Maybe it's easier in California.
clips.script: [admitting, sheepish] I couldn't pull the one at the pond out either. [hopeful, reasoning] ...Maybe it's easier in California.

clips.text: So we bring twenty-four and tell Bernadette it's a tasting menu.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] so we bring twenty-four and tell bernadette [mellow, laid-back, low-key, punchline, deadpan] it's a tasting menu.

clips.text: That's bigger than the golf cart. And it's in Los Angeles. I said Los Angeles.
clips.script: [thrilled, precise] That's bigger than the golf cart. [rising, triumphant] And it's in Los Angeles. [proud, savoring] I said LOS ANGELES.

clips.text: I've seen your stoves. A flame the size of a pea, burning all day and all night so somebody can boil one egg. I'm putting them to work.
clips.script: [scornful, gruff] I've seen your stoves. [withering] A flame the size of a pea, burning all day and all night [contemptuous] so somebody can boil one EGG. [stubborn, final] I'm putting them to work.

clips.text: Then something small and on fire picked a gold thing up off the sidewalk and ran toward the boulevard. I wrote it down as a raccoon. I know it wasn't a raccoon.
clips.script: [crisp, reporting] Then something small and on fire picked a gold thing up off the sidewalk and ran toward the boulevard. [dry, reluctant] I wrote it down as a raccoon. [flat, certain] I know it wasn't a raccoon.

clips.text: Your father says he once baked sixty loaves in one morning. He has never baked.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, dry] Your father says he once baked sixty loaves in one morning. [warm Long Island accent, flat, deadpan] He has NEVER baked.

clips.text: I'm going to be number one.
clips.script: [fierce, certain] I'm going to be NUMBER ONE.

clips.text: You're the one who's always on a plane, Tom. Did you bring this home with you?
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, suspicious, pointed] You're the one who's always on a plane, Tom. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, narrowed, accusing] Did you bring this home with you?

clips.text: The mud gets a muffin and I don't?
clips.script: [thick New York accent, hurt, baffled, punchline] The MUD gets a muffin and I don't?
